spec.intro:
**What this decides.** Whether the standing MAGMA v2 recipe changes its speculative gate — `--spec-min-p 0.7` today, in `strata-iq3_s.json` — and how the M3 metric should read afterwards. This is a one-line change to the adopted config; no engine code is involved.

**Why now.** Measured tonight on a lane verified quiet, same boot, same window, interleaved forward+reverse, on the real-workload 2000-token probe: both lower values win M1 in *every* comparison (0.5 → +11.4% and +7.6%; 0.35 → +4.4% and +11.0%) and both cost ~4.5 points of M3 acceptance **rate** (90.5→85.7, 91.6→87.3). Tokens per window rise from 2.2 to 2.5–2.9, and the chain tests ~1010–1100 drafts instead of ~850 — that is why the rate falls and the throughput rises at the same time.

**Why it is not free.** Your ultimatum says none of the six metrics may regress, and that a change lifting one while lowering another ships only when both numbers are printed side by side and you accept it explicitly. This is that moment. My argument that the M3 fall is a rate artifact — `spec_min_p` only decides how many drafts are *offered*, and every offered draft is still verified against the target's own distribution, so the sampled output cannot change — is a hypothesis about the metric, not a measurement. The measurement is the MMLU/mimic gate.

**What happens with your answers.** The first answer sets the standing config. The follow-ups set whether the quality gate runs before or after the commit, how M3 reads from now on, and whether the harness is allowed to measure on a shared lane. **Nothing is adopted until you answer. Two minutes.**

options.description: Choosing this leaves the standing recipe exactly as it is: no metric up, none down, nothing to gate.
options.insight:
- **Measured tonight:** 0.7 gives M1 159.8 and 146.9 t/s at tokens-per-window 2.18 and 2.09, with M3 acceptance 90.1% and 90.9% (quiet run, same window as both alternatives).
- **The price of safety:** the frontier this round found sits at tokens-per-window 2.5–2.9, so the standing config pays roughly 8–11% of M1 to keep the acceptance rate above 90%.
- **Breaks when:** nothing — this is the safe arm, and it is correct if M3-as-a-rate is a hard constraint rather than a proxy for quality.
- **Here now:** `strata-iq3_s.json` reads `"--spec-min-p", "0.7"`; nothing was adopted tonight.
options.label: Keep 0.7 — no metric moves

options.description: Choosing this sets the gate to 0.5 in the standing config, taking M1 up ~8–11% and the M3 acceptance rate down ~4.5 points.
options.insight:
- **Proven in this window:** 0.5 beat 0.7 in both interleaved passes — 151.9 vs 136.4 t/s (+11.4%) and 145.4 vs 135.1 (+7.6%) — with tokens per window 2.63 and 2.49 against 2.17 and 2.25.
- **The cost, same window:** acceptance 86.8% and 87.8% against 91.2% and 91.9%, because the chain tested 1012 and 969 drafts instead of 849 and 872.
- **Breaks when:** a workload's drafting is already near-certain, where a lower gate buys no extra drafts and only spends window time; the engine's own sweep (`tools/calibrate.py`) exists to find this per machine.
- **Real-world parallel:** vLLM and TensorRT-LLM both expose a draft-acceptance floor for exactly this trade, and both report that the acceptance rate falls while throughput rises once the chain deepens — the rate is a diagnostic, not the objective.
- **Here now:** the standing recipe is unchanged; `campaign/pcie-split-sweep.ps1 -Key spec_min_p` reproduces the whole table in one boot.
options.label: Adopt 0.5 — the best measured M1

options.description: Choosing this sets the gate to 0.35, drafting deepest: the largest tokens-per-window measured (2.96) at the same ~4.5-point acceptance cost.
options.insight:
- **Proven in this window:** 0.35 won every interleaved pass — 166.8 vs 159.8 t/s and 163.1 vs 146.9 — and across both of tonight's runs it won 5 of 6 comparisons with one tie and none lost.
- **Strongest single signal:** tokens per window came out 2.80, 2.96, 2.86, 2.86 on the 0.35 arms against 2.18, 2.09, 2.33, 2.37 on 0.7 — non-overlapping, so the mechanism is not noise even where the t/s gap is.
- **Tradeoff:** the window grows with the chain (12.78 → 14.78/15.84 ms), so part of the extra tokens is spent buying them; at some depth the window cost crosses the gain, and 0.0 was already past that point in the greedy sweep (3.97 tokens at 16.57 ms, 152.8 t/s).
- **Here now:** acceptance 86.6%/84.8% against 90.1%/90.9% — the lowest rate measured tonight.
options.label: Adopt 0.35 — the deepest chain

options.description: Choosing this leaves the config alone while M4 and M5 are measured in the same window, and the adoption decision waits for those numbers.
options.insight:
- **Pattern:** the ultimatum's own adoption gate — baseline six-metric run, then the candidate in the same window, then M1 and M2 at or above baseline and M3–M6 in class.
- **Why it is defensible here:** the invariance argument (offered drafts are verified, so the output cannot change) is a claim about the engine's semantics; an MMLU-Pro and mimic run is a measurement of it, and this campaign has already been burned once by an arm that bent the distribution (`STRATA_BATCH_RESCUE`, MMLU 95.7 → 91.4–92.9).
- **Cost:** one more boot and two graded runs before the config can move, and the lane must be quiet for both.
- **Here now:** MMLU-Pro stands at 95.7 (16:48 today) and mimic was last measured on the T1e boot; neither has been re-run since tonight's measurements.
options.label: Gate first: measure MMLU-Pro and mimic, then decide

options.description: Choosing this leaves the gate alone and spends the effort on the R17 draft head, raising how often each draft is accepted rather than testing more of them.
options.insight:
- **The distinction that matters:** tonight's lever lengthens the chain the stock head already produces; the R17 workstream would make each draft likelier to be right, which raises throughput with no acceptance-rate cost at all.
- **Where it stands:** the R17 chain is validated at 85.4% stock round-trip and its distilled checkpoint reached 57.4% against the stock 85.4%, blocked on the mixed-KV conditioning mismatch — hours of training work, not a config line.
- **Breaks when:** the head is trained on conditioning that does not match decode-time KV state, which is exactly the current blocker; three fix directions are documented.
- **Here now:** the acceptance axis is a multiplier on top of the window law, and the window law now says each extra banked token costs ~1.7 ms against a ~4 ms average.
options.label: Keep 0.7 and attack acceptance instead

options.description: Choosing this takes the throughput and changes the standing metric from acceptance rate to tokens per window, so the scoreboard measures what the engine is for.
options.insight:
- **The case for it:** acceptance rate is a ratio whose denominator grows as the chain deepens, so it falls whenever the engine is made to draft more aggressively — it cannot distinguish 'worse drafts' from 'more drafts'.
- **The case against it:** the ultimatum's own words are that a change lifting one metric while lowering another is a trade, and redefining the metric is the one move that can make any trade disappear; if M3 is redefined it must be recorded as a metric change with a dated entry, not as a win.
- **Real-world handle:** production engines report accepted tokens per step alongside the rate for exactly this reason, and this engine already prints both — `T` and `tokens/window` sit in the same decode-timing line as the acceptance count.
- **Here now:** the engine's line `strata decode timing: ... avg T 2.80, ... tokens/window` and the request line `drafts accepted 1055 of ...` are both in `strata-iq3_s.log` for every request tonight.
options.label: Adopt 0.5 and redefine M3 as tokens-per-window

minp_choice.prompt: The speculative gate `--spec-min-p` is the draft-probability floor: below it, the engine stops extending a verify window. It stands at 0.7 today. Both measured alternatives lift M1 in every interleaved comparison and both cost ~4.5 points of M3 acceptance rate. What should the standing recipe carry?

options.description: Choosing this runs both graded suites first and holds the config change until they come back at or above their standing values.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** the only evidence that can refute the invariance argument, on the two metrics that measure the model rather than the scheduler.
- **Cost:** one boot plus two suites on a quiet lane, and both suites need the lane exclusively.
- **Breaks when:** the suites need traffic the lane cannot serve concurrently; tonight's log already showed a parallel program sharing port 8081, so the run must be gated on a quiet-lane check.
options.label: Yes — both, before the commit

options.description: Choosing this runs the graded knowledge suite alone and accepts mimic on the invariance argument.
options.insight:
- **Why it is reasonable:** MMLU-Pro is the metric this campaign has actually seen bend (the batch-rescue arm took it 95.7 → 91.4–92.9), while mimic has never moved on a scheduling arm.
- **Cost:** roughly half the gating time.
- **Breaks when:** a change alters decoding in a way that shows up as compliance or formatting rather than knowledge — which mimic is there to catch.
options.label: Yes — MMLU-Pro only

options.description: Choosing this adopts on the measured throughput and the invariance argument, and schedules the graded suites afterwards.
options.insight:
- **The argument it rests on:** a draft that is rejected never reaches the output, and a draft that is accepted is the token the target itself would have sampled, so the emitted sequence is the same as without speculation.
- **The risk:** the argument is a claim about semantics and has not been measured on this build tonight; if it is wrong the error lands in the two quality metrics and nowhere else.
- **Cheapest insurance:** the suites can still run on the next boot, and the change is one config line to revert.
options.label: No — commit now, re-measure later

options.description: Choosing this adopts now and records the change as provisional, to be confirmed or reverted after one session of real use.
options.insight:
- **Pattern:** the ultimatum's completion criteria already require the bar to hold over three stable consecutive sessions, so a provisional flag matches the standing law rather than weakening it.
- **Cost:** the recipe is not yet the 'adopted' recipe while flagged, which matters if the lane is handed back mid-flag.
- **Breaks when:** the flag outlives the session it was meant to cover — which is why it carries an expiry.
options.label: No — and mark the adoption provisional for one session

options.description: Choosing this runs the graded suites and re-anchors all six metrics in one window before the commit.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** a baseline row for the chart that covers every metric at once, which is what the trend law asks each session to carry.
- **Cost:** the longest gate on the menu, and the concurrency probes need the lane to itself.
- **Here now:** tonight's M1 window already reads 157.8 t/s at 13.29 ms and the pair 110.7, so the baseline half is partly paid for.
options.label: Yes — both, plus the full six-metric probe

q_gate.prompt: Before the config change is committed, should MMLU-Pro and mimic be measured in the same window?

options.description: Choosing this gates the value with the best measured M1 tonight.
options.insight:
- **Measured:** +11.4% and +7.6% on M1 in two interleaved passes, at a 4.3-point acceptance-rate cost.
- **Why it is the natural first gate:** it is the middle of the measured frontier, so a pass there implies the more aggressive value is worth testing next.
- **Here now:** nothing adopted; the gate would be the first measurement of M4/M5 against this knob.

options.description: Choosing this gates the deepest chain measured.
options.insight:
- **Measured:** tokens per window 2.80–2.96 against 2.09–2.41 for the standing value, winning 5 of 6 interleaved comparisons.
- **Why gate this one:** it is the largest effect, so a quality pass here covers the whole range below 0.7.
- **Cost:** the lowest acceptance rate measured tonight (84.8%).

options.description: Choosing this gates both candidate values so the decision can pick between them on quality as well as speed.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** the two values measured within 3% of each other on M1, so quality is the only remaining discriminator.
- **Cost:** two graded suites per value.
- **Here now:** both are reproducible in one boot with the sweep instrument.
options.label: Both 0.5 and 0.35

options.description: Choosing this gates a value between the standing 0.7 and the measured candidates, taking a smaller share of the effect.
options.insight:
- **Why it exists:** if the acceptance-rate cost is linear in chain depth, half the step takes half the cost.
- **Unmeasured:** 0.6 has not been run tonight, so its tokens per window and rate are unknown; the instrument measures it in about thirty seconds.
- **Breaks when:** the chain gate is not binding for that content, in which case 0.6 and 0.7 measure the same.
options.label: 0.6 — a smaller step than either

options.description: Choosing this lets the engine's own calibration tool pick the value and the PCIe share together, on the live engine without restarts.
options.insight:
- **Why it is a real option:** `tools/calibrate.py` already sweeps `pcie_frac` over seven values and `spec_min_p` over three on a running engine, and reports the pair it picks — that is the engine's own opinion, measured on this machine.
- **What tonight adds to it:** the sweep here showed the split is worth ±4% and the gate is worth +8–11%, so the calibrator's two axes are not equally valuable and its min-p grid stops at 0.3 while tonight's best sat between 0.35 and 0.5.
- **Cost:** a calibration run, plus the gate on whatever it picks.
- **Here now:** the standing config bypasses the calibrator entirely — `--pcie-frac 0.35` is explicit, which also stops the link probe from ever running.
options.label: Let tools/calibrate.py pick it on the live engine

q_gate_which.prompt: The gate is to be run before the decision. Which gate value should it be run on?

options.description: Choosing this makes every probe check for a foreign request first and abort rather than record a contaminated number.
options.insight:
- **Why it matters:** two rounds of this campaign were voided by a shared lane, and one of tonight's candidates had to be re-run for exactly this reason.
- **Cheapest implementation:** the engine log's request lines are the witness — count them across a fixed idle window before and after a probe.
- **Cost:** probes occasionally refuse to run when the operator is chatting with the model, which is the point.
options.label: Hard refuse — stop the run and say why

options.description: Choosing this lets the run proceed but stamps every result with the lane's occupancy.
options.insight:
- **Why it is often enough:** the numbers stay usable when the reader knows the lane was shared, and the check is one line in each instrument.
- **Breaks when:** a result is quoted later without its stamp.
options.label: Warn and record the lane state with every number

options.description: Choosing this keeps the current practice: arms interleaved forward and reversed, so a shared lane adds noise rather than bias.
options.insight:
- **The argument:** interleaving protects the comparison even when the lane is busy, which is why tonight's arm effect reproduced causally while the absolutes were suspect.
- **Breaks when:** the effect is smaller than the contamination, which is exactly the ±5% band this campaign keeps meeting.
options.label: No — the interleaved design already controls it

options.description: Choosing this makes each measurement program claim a lease in the workspace and refuse to start if another holds it.
options.insight:
- **Why a lease rather than a check:** it stops two of my own sessions from starting at all, which is the actual failure mode seen tonight.
- **Cost:** a stale lease after a crash needs an expiry, or the lane locks itself out.
options.label: Add a lane lease file

options.description: Choosing this keeps the measurement protocol as it is and coordinates quiet windows by hand when a result matters.
options.insight:
- **Why it is defensible:** the operator can simply not use the model while a gate runs, which is cheaper than building enforcement.
- **Breaks when:** a session runs unattended, which is exactly when tonight's contamination happened — no one was watching the lane at 19:36.
- **Here now:** the lane is quiet as of 19:45, verified by a 12-second idle check on the engine log.
options.label: No mechanism — coordinate quiet windows manually

q_lane.prompt: Tonight the engine log held 90 request lines for this boot against the ~29–38 I issued, so a parallel program shared port 8081 for part of it. Should the harness refuse to measure while another client is active?

options.description: Choosing this keeps M3 as accepted drafts divided by tested drafts, unchanged.
options.insight:
- **What it measures:** how often an offered draft is right, which falls whenever the chain deepens.
- **Consequence:** every chain-lengthening change will read as an M3 regression even when it makes the engine faster.
- **Here now:** tonight's table is the first case of exactly that.
options.label: Acceptance rate as it is today

options.description: Choosing this makes M3 the tokens the engine banks per verify window, which is what throughput is made of.
options.insight:
- **Measured range tonight:** 2.09–2.18 at the standing gate against 2.49–2.96 at the candidates.
- **Why it fits the scoreboard:** it is the one number that both the chain depth and the acceptance rate feed into, so it cannot be gamed by either alone.
- **Must be recorded as a metric change,** with a dated entry, not as a win.
options.label: Tokens per window

options.description: Choosing this keeps the rate and adds tokens per window, requiring both in every report.
options.insight:
- **Pattern:** the engine already prints both in one line, so the cost is zero and no past number loses its meaning.
- **Breaks when:** a reader picks whichever of the two looks better; the report has to state which is the objective.
options.label: Both, printed side by side every time

options.description: Choosing this measures banked drafts per window rather than the ratio.
options.insight:
- **Why it is close to right:** it counts accepted drafts without dividing by a denominator that grows with aggressiveness.
- **Tradeoff:** it differs from tokens per window by exactly the bonus token, so the two are not interchangeable.
options.label: Accepted drafts per window

options.description: Choosing this removes acceptance from the scoreboard entirely.
options.insight:
- **Not recommended:** the metric exists because a broken drafter once looked fast while accepting almost nothing.
- **Breaks when:** a head regresses and the throughput is masked by a deeper chain — the exact failure M3 was added for.
options.label: Drop M3 and keep five metrics

q_m3def.prompt: If M3 changes meaning, how should it read from now on?

options.description: Choosing this trains the head on windows whose KV positions match decode-time reality.
options.insight:
- **Why first:** it is the cheapest of the three and needs no engine change, only a different data construction.
- **Blocker it targets:** the head currently sees conditioning that does not match the KV state it meets at decode time.
- **Cost:** one training run plus a boot gate.
options.label: Real-position windows

options.description: Choosing this captures the engine's real decode-time state and trains on it directly.
options.insight:
- **Why it is the most faithful:** it removes the mismatch by construction rather than approximating it.
- **Cost:** new dump plumbing in the engine plus the training run, the largest of the three.
options.label: Engine-state dumps

options.description: Choosing this trains the head against the target's own decode-time distribution rather than offline targets.
options.insight:
- **Measured context:** the distilled checkpoint reached 57.4% against the stock head's 85.4%, so the current distillation path is losing badly to the stock head.
- **Why on-policy:** it is the standard fix when a distilled drafter underperforms because its training distribution drifts from inference.
options.label: On-policy distillation

options.description: Choosing this works the three directions sequentially, cheapest first, with a boot gate on each.
options.insight:
- **Pattern:** each earlier step makes the later one cheaper to evaluate, and the chain is already validated at 85.4% stock round-trip.
- **Cost:** the longest path, measured in training runs rather than minutes.
options.label: All three, in that order

options.description: Choosing this leaves the head workstream for later and keeps working the measured configuration space.
options.insight:
- **Measured tonight:** the standing config sits below the frontier the sweep found, and the marginal banked token costs ~1.7 ms against a ~4 ms average, so configuration still has room.
- **Risk of parking:** the head is the only lever that raises acceptance itself, and the configuration levers have now all been measured against it.
options.label: Park it — the config frontier is not exhausted

q_r17.prompt: The R17 draft-head workstream has three documented directions for the mixed-KV conditioning blocker. Which should be tried first?

quick.description: No metric moves; the frontier stays unexploited until the head workstream lands.
quick.label: Keep the acceptance rate: stay at 0.7

quick.description: The measured +8–11% on M1, with the quality suites run before the config moves.
quick.label: Take the throughput and gate it: 0.5, MMLU + mimic first

quick.description: Adopt on the invariance argument, keep the graded suites for the next boot.
quick.label: Take the throughput now: 0.5, re-measure later

quick.description: Both candidates are within 3% on M1, so quality becomes the discriminator.
quick.label: Gate both values, then pick on quality: 0.5 and 0.35

quick.description: Raise how often each draft is right instead of testing more drafts.
quick.label: Leave the gate alone and train the head
